title: Coherator adjunction and detection by global sections
statement: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme Y, let D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y) be the quasi-coherent full subcategory of D(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category]. The inclusion D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y)\hookrightarrow D(\mathcal O_Y) has a right adjoint DQ_Y, so for M\in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y) and E\in D(\mathcal O_Y) there is a natural bijection Hom_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(M,E)\cong Hom_{D_QCoh(\mathcal O_Y)}(M,DQ_Y E). Consequently, if u:E\to E' induces an isomorphism DQ_Y(u), then R\Gamma(Y,u):R\Gamma(Y,E)\to R\Gamma(Y,E') is a quasi-isomorphism; indeed H^i(Y,E)=Hom_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(\mathcal O_Y[-i],E) and \mathcal O_Y[-i] is quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Obtain the inherited triangulated structure, u-indexed coproducts and compact generation from schemeDerivedQCoh_compactlyGenerated. The ambient category has u-indexed coproducts by derivedAmbientHasCoproducts, and schemeDerivedQCohClosedUnderCoproducts makes the full inclusion preserve them. SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian and the proved K-injective-resolution library make the ambient derived category locally u-small; the full subcategory is locally u-small as well. Apply brownHomRepresentabilityLocallySmall to the inclusion for each ambient object, and use Mathlib isLeftAdjoint_of_rightAdjointObjIsDefined_eq_top to assemble its right adjoint. The adjunction supplies the required natural Hom bijections.

Mathlib singleFunctors.shiftIso identifies O_Y[-i] with the degree-i single complex. Its degree-i homology is O_Y via singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso, and O_Y is quasi-coherent by the proved source-library isQuasicoherent_unit. In all other degrees, homologyFunctorFactors and isZero_single_obj_homology identify its homology with a zero object. The empty quasi-coherent coproduct is zero: Sigma.hom_ext proves its identity is zero, so transport quasi-coherence of this empty sum to the homology object. This includes every integer degree and the empty scheme.

Build the additive unitSectionsEquiv by evaluating a unit-module morphism at 1 on the total open. Its inverse extends a global section by restriction to every open and applies unitHomEquiv; the section compatibility and inverse identities are proved explicitly. Cochain.fromSingleEquiv gives an isomorphism between the Hom complex from the degree-zero unit single complex and the underlying additive global-sections complex. The leftHomologyData homology isomorphism identifies its cohomology with CohomologyClass. CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv identifies classes with homotopy morphisms into the shifted K-injective target. Qh_map_bijective supplies the additive derived Hom equivalence; quotientCompQhIso and Q.commShiftIso transport it to the stated localization model. The additive Hom equivalence of the (-i,i) shift adjunction shifts the source instead of the target. Finally mapHomologyIso for forgetting module structure gives the requested additive equivalence from the module-valued global cohomology.

Prove naturality of both comparisons on actual maps. Postcomposition defines a map of Hom complexes and of cohomology classes; an explicit LeftHomologyMapData proves compatibility with leftHomologyData. The degreewise unitSectionsEquiv and Cochain.fromSingleMk_postcomp prove naturality of the sections-complex isomorphism, hence of unitClassSectionsIso. On derived Hom, Cocycle.equivHomShift_symm_postcomp, quotientCompQhIso naturality, Q.commShiftIso naturality, and the shift adjunction Hom naturality prove unitClassDerivedEquiv_naturality. For O_Y[-i] in the full subcategory, the given adjunction conjugates postcomposition by Q(f) to postcomposition by DQ_Y(Q(f)), a bijection since the latter is an isomorphism. Naturality of unitClassDerivedEquiv gives bijectivity of the cohomology-class postcomposition map. Naturality of unitClassSectionsIso then gives an isomorphism on each underlying global cohomology object. The forgetful functor from modules reflects isomorphisms and preserves homology, so quasiIso_map_iff_of_preservesHomology proves the required module-valued quasi-isomorphism.
